schedule.note: Company rule 5,000 mi. OM p. 286: never past 15,000 mi or 12 months (or 500 hours). Check oil level every 3,000 mi. Cartridge filter Mopar 68677810AA or Fleetguard LF16453. 10W-30 CK-4 (MS-10902) above 0 F, 5W-40 below (OM p. 350).
OM p. 291: every 7,500 mi or 6 months, and at the first sign of irregular wear (p. 287). Lug nuts 134-149 ft-lb, re-check after 25 mi (OM p. 355-356).
OM pp. 292-293: front and rear engine fuel filters every 15,000 mi or 12 months. Front 3 micron, rear 5 micron. Water in Fuel light on: drain before starting (OM p. 169).

schedule.item: Engine air filter (inspect, replace if needed)
schedule.note: OM p. 291: inspect and replace if necessary every 15,000 mi or 12 months; never past 30,000 mi or 24 months. Inspect at each oil change in dust (p. 287).

schedule.item: Front end, CV and U-joints, suspension check
schedule.note: OM p. 291-292: front end lube and CV/U-joints every 7,500 mi or 6 months; front suspension, tie rods and boots every 15,000 mi or 12 months.

schedule.item: Brake linings and parking brake inspection
schedule.note: OM p. 292: linings and parking brake every 22,500 mi or 18 months; brakes also on the monthly list (p. 287). Heavy towing wears pads faster.

schedule.item: Front and rear axle fluid (change, frequent towing)
schedule.note: OM p. 293: every 22,500 mi or 18 months; change the fluid for frequent trailer towing. Rear 12.0 in DRW axle: pre-mixed Mopar 75W-140 only; front 75W-85 (OM p. 353).
OM p. 293: inspect every 30,000 mi or 24 months, change for frequent trailer towing; routine change 60,000 mi. Mopar BW44-44 (p. 353).
OM p. 293: ATF 818 change at 60,000 mi or 48 months. Use TOW/HAUL when towing to cut heat and shifting (OM p. 208). Ask if this truck needs the Ram 2026 Cummins transmission software update.
OM p. 293: CCV filter at 75,000 mi or 60 months, or when the cluster shows Perform Service (p. 287).
OM p. 294: flush power steering fluid at 97,500 mi or 78 months.
OM p. 294: 150,000 mi or 10 years, dealer recommended. Mopar OAT only, 22 qt (OM pp. 349, 354).
No annual inspection report on file. Totni (the carrier) should hold it. Ask Totni, or get one at a shop that does 396.17 inspections.

Big Tex OM p. 59 and Dexter p. 5: adjust at the first 200 mi, then every 3,000 mi (Dexter p. 4: 3 months or 3,000 mi). Self-adjusting brakes adjust with hard reverse stops (Big Tex p. 64). No 200 mi adjustment on record.

schedule.item: Hub bearings: repack grease or change hub oil
schedule.note: Dexter p. 57-58: grease or hub oil every 12 months or 12,000 mi (was 15,000 mi from the dealer; the manual is stricter). Big Tex OM p. 62, 69: unsealed bearings yearly or 12,000 mi.

schedule.item: Gooseneck coupler, latch, safety chains, breakaway
schedule.note: Big Tex OM p. 61: check ball and coupler for cracks, pits, flats; grease; check the lock before each use. Check coupler tightness after the first 50 mi (p. 21). Ram factory gooseneck hitch: 37,100 lb trailer, 5,565 lb pin (OM p. 200).
Dexter p. 4: trailer brake wiring every 12 months. Every trip: use the Ram trailer light check in the Trailer Tow menu (OM p. 207).

schedule.item: Ramps, dovetail, deck bolts and hinges
schedule.note: Check hinges, springs and welds.
Plan is every 6 to 12 months. Due at the 6 month mark.

schedule.item: Tire age limit (replace by DOT date + 6 yr)
schedule.note: Industry guideline, not a Big Tex or TrailerGard term. Read the DOT date code on each sidewall. Trailer built Aug 2026.
No annual inspection report on file. Inspect the trailer with the truck.
OM p. 355: DRW flanged two-piece M14 x 1.50 nuts, 22 mm socket: min 134, nominal 142, max 149 ft-lb. Retighten after 25 mi after any wheel work (p. 356). Do not oil studs.
OM p. 287 monthly list plus: tire pressure incl. spare monthly (p. 327), oil level every 3,000 mi (p. 286), DEF level (p. 291).

Dexter 9-15K p. 76: torque before first use and after any wheel removal, re-check at 50 and 100 mi; Big Tex OM p. 59: 10, 25 and 50 mi. Dexter p. 4: every 3 months or 3,000 mi. Torque depends on the nut type (see SOP).
Big Tex OM p. 61 and Dexter p. 4: before every use. Logged monthly here.

schedule.item: Trailer tire pressure and condition (80 psi cold)
schedule.note: Big Tex OM p. 58, 67: inflate cold to the trailer VIN/certification label pressure (80 psi for ST235/80R16 LRE). Dexter p. 4: weekly. Also every pre-trip.

schedule.item: Brake magnets and controller output check
schedule.note: Dexter p. 4 and Big Tex OM p. 62: magnets for wear and current draw, controller output and modulation every 6 months or 6,000 mi.

schedule.item: Brake shoes, drums and wiring (annual, by dealer)
schedule.note: Dexter p. 4: linings, drums, brake wiring every 12 months or 12,000 mi. Big Tex OM p. 64-65: dealer inspection of brakes and magnets at least yearly.
Dexter p. 4, 66: suspension parts every 6,000 mi or 6 months; springs and hanger welds yearly. Big Tex OM p. 62: axle attachment bolts checked by the dealer yearly.
Big Tex OM p. 62, 67: grease the gears in the top of the jacks once a year; use the grease fitting if there is one.
Big Tex OM p. 62: rotate at 5,000 mi; inspect tread and sidewalls every 6 months or 6,000 mi.

schedule.item: S5 coupler lock and Trimax puck lock (lube, key handling)
schedule.note: On-hand theft protection: S5 Coupler Locks steel box sleeve over the Demco coupler, Trimax THP XL puck lock in the side shroud. Lube the puck lock every 3 months. Keep the key off the trailer and a spare at home. Key codes are not stored in this app.

pretrip_truck.title: Pre-trip: truck
items: Engine oil level, on level ground (Ram OM p. 286-287)
Coolant reservoir and DEF level; DEF 2 gal max from jugs at half (p. 197)
Tires cold to door placard, look for damage; no towing on a compact spare, 50 mph max on a full spare (p. 204, 327)
Lug nuts: 142 ft-lb if any wheel was off; re-check at 25 mi (p. 355-356)
Lights and wipers, mirrors extended (p. 287)
No warning lights: Water in Fuel, Wait to Start, DPF (p. 132, 169)
Warm up before load; avoid long idling (p. 172, 297)
TOW/HAUL on; exhaust brake on, never on ice (p. 177, 200)

pretrip_trailer.title: Pre-trip: trailer and hitch
items: Remove S5 coupler lock before hitching, stow in toolbox
Ball and receiver greased, no cracks or flats; latch closed and pinned; jack-lift test 1 in (Big Tex p. 45-46, 61)
Drop legs fully up and pinned (p. 46)
Safety chains to bed receivers, not the ball, with turn slack (p. 47)
Breakaway lanyard to truck, test pull, pin back in (p. 48)
Tires 80 psi cold, no cuts or bulges (p. 58, 61)
Lug nuts tight; 10/25/50 mi re-check after wheel work (p. 59, 61)
7-pin plugged in, trailer brake type and GAIN set (Ram OM p. 205-206)
Run the Ram trailer light check: turn, brake, marker (Ram OM p. 207)
Cargo 60% in front half, low and centered, tied down (Big Tex p. 55)
Ramps and dovetail stowed and latched (p. 56)
Scale it if 12,501+ lb cargo: GVWR, GAWR, GCWR, pin (Ram OM p. 204)

enroute.title: Every stop (about once an hour)
items: Coupler still locked; re-check it after the first 50 mi (Big Tex p. 21)
Plugs connected, chain and lanyard slack right (p. 21)
Tires not visibly low; hubs not hot to the touch (p. 21, 68)
Cargo and straps tight (p. 21)
Under 60 mph towing (Big Tex p. 21)

posttrip.title: Post-trip and shutdown
items: Idle 3-5 min after full-load or uphill running before shutdown (Ram OM p. 173)
Let a DPF regen finish if the cluster says regen in process (p. 132-133)
Top up DEF; do not overfill in freezing weather (p. 196-197)
Walk around: tires, hubs, lights, leaks, straps stowed
Park level; parking brake, PARK; never park on a grade with the trailer (p. 204)
Note any lug nut, brake or light issue in the Log
Plug in the block heater below 0 F (required below -20 F, 1+ h) (p. 175)
Write down the odometer (Update odometer above)
Install S5 coupler lock with puck lock whenever the trailer is unhooked

monthly.title: Truck: monthly or before a long trip (Ram OM p. 287)
items: Engine oil level (30 min after a warm shutdown)
Interior and exterior lights
Battery terminals and cables
Brake pads, rotors and fluid level
Steering, suspension, axle boots
Wipers, washer fluid
Coolant reservoir
DEF level
Tire pressure incl. spare, cold (OM p. 327)

warranty.ram_src: 2026 Ram HD Warranty Information booklet (mopar.com) and Ram's 2026 10 yr / 100K powertrain release. Read your own booklet for exact terms.
rules: Keep every service receipt (Ram OM p. 287: Retain all receipts).
Follow the severe-duty oil schedule; the manual says towing may shorten it (OM p. 287).
Stay inside GVWR, GAWR, GCWR and hitch ratings (OM p. 197-204).
No Hamilton cam kit while under warranty.
Use Ram-specified oil (MS-10902 CK-4), OAT coolant only, ATF 818, API-certified DEF (OM p. 349-353). Non-OAT coolant needs a dealer flush (p. 349).
ULSD only; biodiesel above B20 can cause severe damage (OM p. 347-348).
Trailer: log every lug nut torque check with date and miles (Big Tex OM p. 70). Normal wear items are not covered (p. 71).
warranty.lds: Separate dealer mechanical warranty (Louisiana Dealer Services, 48 months or 150,000 mi) allows company use with a single driver. It prohibits multiple drivers and overloading. Contract copy not on file.
warranty.tire_note: Trailer tires and wheels: TrailerGard 7 years to 10/5/2033, commercial use, no deductible. Before any tire work the shop must call the warranty company. Only page 1 of 4 is on file. Ram tires: no warranty paperwork on file.

Trailer axle tag: maker (Dexter?), brake type (manual or self-adjust), and whether hubs are grease or oil bath.
Annual DOT inspection reports for the truck and trailer from Totni (or book one).

Photo of the Ram door-jamb tire placard and the certification label (cold psi front/rear, front and rear GAWR).
The CAT scale ticket from 10/7: steer, drive and trailer axle weights, and whether the empty trailer was hooked up for the 10,940 lb.
Trailer wheel nuts: flange nut or cone nut (sets the 150-325 ft-lb torque row).
Rating stamped on the gooseneck ball (must be at least 25,900 lb) and whether the hitch is the Ram factory puck system.
Was the trailer brake 200-mile adjustment ever done? (Big Tex and Dexter require it.)

t-oil.about: Change the Cummins 6.7 engine oil and the cartridge filter. Company rule is every 5,000 mi (Ram manual allows 15,000 mi or 12 months, severe-duty towing 7,500 mi or 6 months).
tools: Filter cap socket for the cartridge housing
parts: 12 qt 10W-30 API CK-4 oil (MS-10902, such as Mopar, Rotella, Rimula)
Cartridge filter Mopar 68677810AA or Fleetguard LF16453 (the spin-on Donaldson DBL7349 does not fit)
New filter o-rings and drain plug washer
specs: 15,000 mi or 12 months or 500 h, sooner if the indicator says (OM p. 286, 291). Company rule 5,000 mi
Trailer towing and heavy loading may reduce the interval (OM p. 287)
Never past 15,000 mi or 500 h (OM p. 348)
10W-30 CK-4 above 0 F; 5W-40 synthetic below 0 F
At least 30 min after a warm shutdown, on level ground
Ignition ON (do not start), press the accelerator slowly 3 times within 10 seconds, ignition OFF. Some trucks reset in the cluster menu
Drain plug and filter cap torque
Not in the owner's manual. Use the number in the dealer service information or the cap/housing marking
steps: Park on level ground, set the brake, chock the wheels. Run the engine a few minutes to warm the oil, then shut off.
Raise the front on ramps or stands if you need room. Slide the drain pan under the sump.
Remove the drain plug and let the oil drain fully (10+ minutes). Wipe and refit the plug with a new washer, then torque to spec.
Remove the oil filter cap from the housing on top of the engine, lift out the old cartridge and let it drip dry.
Fit the new cartridge and new o-rings (wet them with fresh oil). Refit the cap and torque to the marked spec.
Pour in about 11 qt of 10W-30, wait a minute, then check the dipstick.
Start the engine, watch for the oil pressure light to go out, check for leaks at the plug and cap, shut off and wait 5 minutes.
Top up to the full mark. Do not overfill.
Reset the oil change indicator (see specs).
Log it here: date, odometer, shop or who, cost. Keep the receipt (warranty requires proof of the severe-duty schedule).
safety: Hot oil burns. Let the engine cool a few minutes before draining.
Use jack stands rated for the load. Never work under a vehicle held only by a jack.
Recycle the used oil and the filter at a shop or parts store.
Use Ram-specified oil only while under warranty (10W-30 or the 5W-40 for cold). No switch to 15W-40 until off the factory lifters.
cite: Ram OM p. 286-287 (intervals, level check, severe service, keep receipts)

t-rot.about: Rotate the tires and look them over. Ram diesel plan: every 7,500 mi, and at the first sign of uneven wear.
tools: Torque wrench with the right socket
specs: Every 7,500 mi or 6 months; sooner at the first sign of irregular wear (OM p. 287, 291)
Flanged two-piece M14 x 1.50 nuts, 22 mm hex deep socket: min 134, nominal 142, max 149 ft-lb (OM p. 355)
Star pattern for 8 or 10 nuts, tighten in steps to final torque (OM p. 356)
Clean the nut-to-washer face of the two-piece nuts at each rotation (OM p. 355)
Door-jamb placard, cold (OM p. 327). About 1 psi per 12 F change (p. 331)
steps: Check cold pressures first and write them down (door-jamb label sets the target for the load).
Chalk the tires with where they sit (position and direction).
Loosen the lug nuts one turn while the wheel is on the ground.
Jack at the frame point, set stands. Never lift on the axle tube alone for a long job.
Remove wheels. Look at the tread, sidewalls and valve stems. Check brake pads and rotors while the wheel is off (see the brake item).
Move the wheels using the pattern your tire shop or the dealer recommends for dual rear wheels (general guidance, ask which one they want for these tires).
Refit and snug in a star pattern, lower the truck, then torque in a star pattern in steps to 142 ft-lb (134-149).
Reset pressures. Re-check the torque after 25 miles (OM p. 356).
Log date and odometer.
safety: Use jack stands rated for the load. Never work under a vehicle held only by a jack.
Never overtighten with an impact gun: it stretches studs and warps rotors.
Dually wheels must be seated and the duals spaced so they do not touch.
t-rot.note: The dual-wheel rotation pattern is general guidance. Torque and interval are from the owner's manual.
cite: Ram OM p. 355-356 (lug torque, pattern, 25 mi re-check)

t-lug.about: Check the Ram dually wheel nuts with a torque wrench: 142 ft-lb nominal (134-149), and again 25 miles after any wheel work.
tools: 22 mm six-sided deep wall socket (thin-wall if needed for the duals)
specs: Flanged two-piece M14 x 1.50 nuts, 22 mm hex deep socket: min 134, nominal 142, max 149 ft-lb (OM p. 355)
Seat all nuts, then tighten in increments, star pattern, opposite nut each time (OM p. 356)
Clean the nut and washer faces instead (OM p. 355)
steps: Truck parked and cold, wheels on the ground (do not torque fully with the truck on a jack, OM p. 356).
Set the wrench to 142 ft-lb.
Pull each nut in the star pattern until it clicks. Do not keep pulling after the click.
If any nut turns before the click, note which one and recheck all nuts on that wheel.
Look at studs and nut seats for rust streaks or cracks.
Log date and odometer.
safety: A loose dually wheel can come off. If a nut keeps losing torque, have a shop check the studs and wheel.
t-lug.note: From the owner's manual. Our DRW uses flanged nuts.
cite: Ram OM p. 355 (torque table, socket, two-piece nuts)
Ram OM p. 356 (pattern, retighten after 25 mi)

t-fuel.about: Replace both engine-mounted fuel filters at 15,000 mi.
specs: Front and rear filters every 15,000 mi or 12 months (OM p. 292-293)
2025-26 canisters can trap air after a change
Do not start the engine until the water is drained from the filters (OM p. 169-170)
Ignition ON 30 s, OFF 30 s, three times before cranking (OM p. 194)
steps: Engine off and cool. Disconnect nothing electrical unless the service information says so. Have rags ready for fuel.
Drain the filter housing water separator drain if equipped, into a pan.
Remove the old element from each housing. Keep track of which is front and rear.
Lightly oil the new o-rings with clean diesel, fit the new elements and close the caps by hand to the marked torque.
Prime the system: key ON for a few seconds, off, repeat per the dealer procedure, until the pump quiets.
Start the engine. If it cranks long or stumbles, shut off and prime again (air trap).
Check for leaks, then log date, odometer, shop and cost.
safety: No flames or sparks. Wipe all spilled fuel.
Use only filters that meet the stated micron ratings. A wrong filter harms the injection system.
t-fuel.note: Prime sequence is general guidance. Ask the dealer for the priming steps for this VIN.
cite: Ram OM p. 194 (out of fuel priming)
Ram OM p. 347, 351 (ULSD only, B20 max)

t-air.about: Inspect the engine air filter every 15,000 mi or 12 months and replace it if dirty. Never run it past 30,000 mi or 24 months.
parts: Mopar or equal air filter element
specs: Every 15,000 mi or 12 months, replace if necessary (OM p. 291)
Inspect at each oil change (OM p. 287)
steps: Engine off. Unclip the air box lid.
Pull the element and hold it to a light. If you cannot see light through the paper, replace it.
Wipe dust out of the air box. Do not blow dirt toward the intake tube.
Fit the new element, seat it flat, close and latch the lid.
Check the intake hose clamps are tight.
Log date and odometer.
safety: Never run the engine without the filter.
cite: Ram OM p. 291 (interval and 30,000 mi max)

t-cabin.about: Replace the cabin air filter every 12,000 mi.
parts: Cabin air filter for the 2026 Ram 2500/3500
steps: Find the filter door behind or under the glove box (see the owner's manual or video for this model).
Release the glove box stops, open the filter door.
Slide out the old filter. Note the airflow arrow.
Fit the new filter with the arrow pointing the same way.
Close the door and the glove box. Run the fan to check airflow.
Log date and odometer.
safety: None special.

t-front.about: Inspect the front end, CV and U-joints and suspension every 7,500 mi.
tools: Grease gun (if the joints have fittings)
specs: Every 7,500 mi: inspect front end, lubricate if equipped with serviceable fittings, inspect CV and U-joints
Inspect front suspension, tie rod ends and boot seals for cracks, leaks, looseness or end play
steps: Raise the front and set stands.
Grab each front wheel at 12 and 6, then 3 and 9, and rock it. Any clunk or play means a worn tie rod, ball joint or bearing.
Look at all rubber boots (tie rod ends, axle shafts) for cracks or grease leaks.
Grease any fitting that has one, until fresh grease just shows.
Check the U-joints on the driveshafts for rust dust or play.
Look for leaking shocks and loose bolts.
Log date, odometer and anything found.
safety: Use jack stands rated for the load. Never work under a vehicle held only by a jack.
A loose steering part is a safety item. Do not drive on it.
cite: Ram OM p. 291 (front end lube, 7,500 mi / 6 mo)
Ram OM p. 292 (CV/U-joints; front suspension 15,000 mi / 12 mo)

t-brake.about: Inspect brake linings and the parking brake. Heavy towing wears them faster than the 22,500 mi manual interval.
specs: Inspect linings and parking brake every 22,500 mi, and look at each oil change
Check pads, rotors, brake operation and fluid level
steps: Check fluid level in the master cylinder and the color of the fluid.
Raise the truck, remove the wheels (see the rotation steps).
Look through the caliper window at pad thickness. Measure it and write it down. Replace pads when they are thin (use the dealer minimum).
Look at the rotors for deep grooves, blue heat marks or a lip at the edge.
Check brake hoses for cracks or bulges.
Check the parking brake holds the truck on a slope.
Refit wheels, torque in a star pattern, log pad thickness, date and odometer.
safety: Use jack stands rated for the load. Never work under a vehicle held only by a jack.
Brake dust is harmful: do not blow it with air. Use brake cleaner.
If the pedal is soft or the truck pulls, stop and have it looked at.

t-belt.about: Inspect the drive belt every 22,500 mi.
specs: Inspect every 22,500 mi, replace as necessary
steps: Engine off. Open the hood.
Look along the belt for cracks, missing ribs, glazing, fraying or oil contamination.
Press the belt midway between pulleys. It should not be loose or sag.
Look at the tensioner and the idler pulleys for wobble or noise.
Replace the belt if cracked or glazed, using the belt routing label.
Log date and odometer.
safety: Keep hands and hair away if the engine is running.

t-axle.about: Change the front and rear axle gear oil. The manual says to change it for frequent trailer towing, at 22,500 mi.
tools: Socket or hex key for fill and drain plugs
parts: Rear (DRW 12.0 axle): Mopar GL-5 synthetic 75W-140, pre-mixed with limited slip additive
Front: SAE 75W-85 HD Ram GL-5 synthetic
RTV or new plug washers if needed
specs: Inspect at 22,500; change for police, taxi, fleet, off-road or frequent trailer towing
Mopar 75W-140 GL-5 synthetic, pre-mixed (no loose additive)
Not in the owner's manual. Use the dealer service information
Dexter: hub grease or oil every 12 months or 12,000 mi (Dexter p. 57-58)
steps: Drive the truck a few miles to warm the gear oil, then park level.
Loosen the FILL plug first (so you can refill before you drain).
Drain through the drain plug (or by removing the cover) into the pan. Look for metal flakes on the magnet.
Clean and refit the plug with a new washer, torque to spec.
Pump new fluid in until it just starts to run out of the fill hole. Do the front and rear separately.
Refit the fill plug and torque.
Wipe clean and check for leaks after a short drive.
Log date, odometer, fluid used, shop and cost.
safety: Use jack stands rated for the load. Never work under a vehicle held only by a jack.
Do not mix fluids. The 3500 DRW rear axle takes only the pre-mixed 75W-140.
Hot gear oil burns.
cite: Ram OM p. 293 (22,500 mi / 18 mo, change for towing)
Ram OM p. 353 (75W-140 pre-mixed rear, 75W-85 front)

t-whl.about: Inspect the wheel bearings at 30,000 mi.
steps: Raise the axle and set stands.
Spin the wheel by hand. Listen for grinding or roughness.
Rock the wheel top to bottom for play (see front-end steps).
Check for leaking seals or grease on the inside of the rim.
Have the dealer measure end play if anything feels wrong.
Log date, odometer and findings.
safety: Use jack stands rated for the load. Never work under a vehicle held only by a jack.

t-tcase.about: Change the transfer case fluid. Manual: inspect at 30,000 mi and change for frequent trailer towing; routine change at 60,000 mi.
tools: Socket for fill and drain plugs
specs: Change at 30,000 mi for frequent towing; 60,000 mi otherwise
Not in the owner's manual. Use the dealer service information
steps: Warm the fluid by driving a few miles, park level.
Loosen the fill plug first.
Remove the drain plug and drain fully. Check the drained fluid for metal.
Refit the drain plug with a new washer, torque to spec.
Pump in new fluid to the bottom of the fill hole.
Refit and torque the fill plug. Check for leaks after a drive.
Log date, odometer, shop and cost.
safety: Use jack stands rated for the load. Never work under a vehicle held only by a jack.
Use only the specified fluid.

t-trans.about: Change the automatic transmission fluid (Torqueflite 8-speed) every 60,000 mi. Heavy towing may call for earlier service: ask the dealer.
tools: Dealer-level fluid exchange or pan drop tools
parts: Transmission filter and pan gasket if the dealer replaces them
specs: Dealer decision. Not stated in the owner's manual
Ask whether this VIN needs the Ram 2026 Cummins transmission software update (built before 2025-12-11)
Use TOW/HAUL in hills; lower gear on steep grades; no cruise on hills or heavy loads (OM p. 208)
steps: This job is best done by the dealer or a diesel shop: the fluid level is set with a scan tool at a set temperature.
Ask them to use ATF 818 only and to check for the software update.
Get the work order: fluid type, level procedure, odometer, price.
Log date, odometer, shop and cost, and keep the work order for the warranty file.
safety: Wrong fluid or a wrong fill level can damage the transmission and the warranty.

t-ccv.about: Replace the crankcase ventilation (CCV) filter at 75,000 mi or when the cluster shows Perform Service.
specs: Every 75,000 mi, or when the cluster says Perform Service
No interval is listed in the owner's manual
steps: Watch for the Perform Service message in the cluster. It means emissions maintenance is due.
Have the dealer replace the CCV element and clear the message (they use service tools).
Ask them to check the DEF system filter and note it on the invoice.
Log date, odometer, shop and cost.
safety: Do not ignore the Perform Service message.

t-ps.about: Flush and replace the power steering fluid at 97,500 mi.
parts: Mopar Power Steering Fluid +4 or ATF+4
specs: Mopar Power Steering Fluid +4 or ATF+4
steps: Check the reservoir level and color each month (see monthly checks).
At the interval, have the shop flush the system with the specified fluid.
Log date, odometer, shop and cost.
safety: Do not top off with other fluids.

t-cool.about: Flush and replace the coolant at 10 years or 150,000 mi, whichever comes first. Check the reservoir monthly.
tools: Dealer or diesel shop for the flush
specs: Mopar OAT 10 Year/150K only. Do not mix with HOAT or global coolant
The manual strongly recommends cooling system work be done by the dealer
Coolant must not pass 240 F; below 140 F for long periods harms the engine (OM p. 173-174)
steps: Monthly: look at the reservoir level with the engine cold. Never open the cap hot.
If you must add, use only Mopar OAT 10 yr coolant (premix 50/50 or add distilled water to a concentrate).
At the interval, have the dealer drain, flush and refill with fresh OAT coolant.
Log date, odometer, shop and cost.
safety: Never open the radiator or reservoir cap on a hot engine.
Do not use water alone or alcohol-based products or rust inhibitors.
cite: Ram OM p. 294 (150,000 mi / 10 yr, dealer)
Ram OM p. 348-351 (OAT only, do not mix)
Ram OM p. 173 (240 F max gauge, 21 psi cap)

t-monthly.about: The Ram owner's manual monthly (or before a long trip) walk-around for the truck.
specs: Once a month or before a long trip
Check pressure of each tire incl. the spare at least monthly, cold, to the door placard (OM p. 327)
steps: Engine oil: check the level 30 minutes after a warm shutdown, truck level.
Lights: walk around with a helper or reflect off a wall: head, tail, brake, turn, clearance.
Battery: look at terminals and cables for corrosion and tightness.
Brakes: look at pads, rotors, feel the pedal, check the fluid level.
Steering, suspension, axle boots: look and listen on a short drive.
Wipers and washer fluid: test and top up.
Coolant reservoir: level OK with the engine cold.
DEF level (7.5 gal tank). Check tire pressures.
Tap the checklist boxes on the tab and log the date.
safety: Do the engine and coolant checks cold.
cite: Ram OM p. 286 (oil level every 3,000 mi)
Ram OM p. 327 (tire pressure monthly incl. spare)

t-dot.about: Get the annual DOT inspection (49 CFR 396.17) for the truck. Under the lease Totni is the carrier, so ask them for a copy first.
specs: Commercial vehicles over 10,000 lb (combination weight counts) in interstate commerce
steps: Ask Totni (Felix or Virginia) if they already have an annual inspection report on this VIN.
If not, call a truck shop or inspection station that does 396.17 annual inspections (federal inspector qualified).
Bring the truck and trailer. Expect brakes, lights, steering, suspension, tires, coupling and frame to be checked.
Get the report and decal. Keep the report in the truck and send a copy to Totni.
Fix any items marked defective, then log it here with the date and the shop.
safety: Do not run interstate without a current report if the carrier requires it.
t-dot.note: Check with Totni for what they require.

r-brake.about: Adjust the trailer electric brakes: after the first 200 miles, then every 3,000 miles or 3 months, and sync the Ram brake controller gain.
tools: Brake spoon or screwdriver (modified 80 degree tool for drop spindles)
specs: After the first 200 miles (Big Tex OM p. 59; Dexter p. 5)
Every 3,000 miles or 3 months (Big Tex p. 59, 64; Dexter p. 4, 14)
Adjust by hard stops in reverse; read the axle tag (Big Tex p. 64)
Brake type Heavy Electric above 10,000 lb; set GAIN just below wheel lockup at 20-25 mph with the manual lever (OM p. 205-206)
steps: Find the axle tag: manual-adjust or self-adjusting. Self-adjusting: do several firm stops in reverse instead, then skip to the gain step.
Park level, chock, jack one wheel by the frame and set a stand (Big Tex p. 63 jack points).
Remove the adjusting-hole cover on the back of the backing plate.
Turn the star wheel to expand the shoes until the wheel is very hard to turn.
Back the star wheel off until the wheel turns freely with a slight drag (Big Tex p. 64; Dexter p. 14).
Refit the cover. Repeat on all 4 brakes.
Lower the trailer. On a dry empty lot at 20-25 mph, squeeze the Ram manual brake lever fully; raise GAIN until just below lockup (OM p. 206).
Log date and trailer miles.
safety: Use jack stands rated for the load. Never work under a vehicle held only by a jack.
Never crawl under the trailer unless it is on firm level ground on jack stands (Big Tex p. 63).
Do not get grease on linings or magnets (Dexter p. 15).
cite: Big Tex OM p. 59 (200 mi, then 3,000 mi; sync)
Big Tex OM p. 64 (manual adjust steps)
Ram OM p. 205-206 (ITBM gain and brake type)

r-hub.about: Service the trailer hub bearings every 12 months or 12,000 miles: repack grease (or change the hub oil if the hubs have clear oil caps). Inspect drums, seals and magnets while the hub is off.
parts: Dexter or equal bearing grease (do not mix grease types)
Gear oil 80/90 if the hubs are oil bath
specs: Grease or hub oil every 12 months or 12,000 mi (Dexter p. 57-58)
Lithium complex NLGI No. 2 EP; do not mix grease types (Dexter p. 57, 59)
SAE 90, 80W-90 or 75W-90 to the line on the cap (Dexter p. 58-59)
Inner nut 100 ft-lb while turning, back off, then per Dexter steps; outer locknut 100-175 ft-lb (Dexter p. 61-62)
Replace any bearing that was under water (Big Tex OM p. 69)
Grease or oil bath is not confirmed. Read the axle tag or look for clear oil caps
steps: Find out if the hubs are grease or oil bath (a rubber plug and a sight window mean oil bath).
Chock, jack by the frame, set stands.
Remove the wheel, dust cap, cotter pin and spindle nut. Pull the hub and drum straight off.
Wipe off old grease. Inspect each bearing and cup. Replace in sets if pitted, blue or rough.
Pack the bearings by hand or with a packer until grease shows through the rollers.
Fit a new seal. Refit the hub, tighten the inner spindle nut to 100 ft-lb while turning, back off, then finish per Dexter p. 61-62 (outer locknut 100-175 ft-lb) and fit a new cotter pin.
Oil bath: drain the old oil, refill to the line on the cap with SAE 90 / 80W-90 / 75W-90.
Check the brake linings and magnets while the drum is off.
Refit the wheel, torque the nuts in a star pattern, re-check at 10, 25 and 50 miles.
Log date and trailer miles.
safety: Use jack stands rated for the load. Never work under a vehicle held only by a jack.
Bearings are replaced in a cone and cup set.
Wash hands: bearing grease and old oil are dirty and irritate skin.
r-hub.note: Steps are general shop practice. Get the Dexter service manual for the exact spindle nut procedure.
cite: Big Tex OM p. 62, 68-69 (yearly or 12,000 mi; water)

r-gn.about: Inspect and grease the gooseneck coupler, latch, safety chains and breakaway cable. General guidance, every 3 months or 3,000 mi.
parts: Lock pin or R-clip if worn
specs: Ball and receiver: cracks, pits, flats; grease; lock works (Big Tex OM p. 61)
After the first 50 mi of a tow
2-5/16 in Demco EZ Latch (Big Tex spec sheet). Ball must match size and be rated at least the trailer GVWR 25,900 lb (Big Tex p. 42)
37,100 lb trailer, 5,565 lb pin weight (OM p. 200)
To the bed safety chain receivers, never to the ball or its support; slack for turns but keep the neck on the bed (Big Tex p. 47)
Coupler height bolts tight, then jam nuts; do not over-tighten (Big Tex p. 42)
Remove the S5 sleeve and puck lock before hitching; stow in the toolbox. Reinstall whenever the trailer is unhooked (see the S5 coupler lock SOP).
steps: Remove the S5 coupler lock and stow it in the toolbox before you couple. Reinstall it whenever the trailer is unhooked (see the S5 coupler lock SOP).
Wipe the receiver, look and feel for cracks, worn spots and pits (Big Tex p. 45).
Grease the inside of the receiver and the ball with automotive bearing grease (p. 45, 66).
Couple: lower onto the ball, close and pin the latch, then use the jack to raise the truck about 1 in to prove the lock (p. 45-46). Do not lift more than 1 in.
Raise the drop legs fully; keep feet clear, they spring up (p. 46).
Hook chains to the bed receivers with turn slack (p. 47).
Breakaway lanyard to the truck so the pin pulls before the chains go tight; not to a chain or the ball (p. 48).
Check the height-adjust bolts and jam nuts.
Log date and trailer miles.
safety: A coupler that pops off the ball is dangerous. Do not tow with a worn latch.
cite: Big Tex OM p. 42-49 (gooseneck coupling, chains, breakaway)
Big Tex OM p. 61, 66 (before each use, grease)
Big Tex OM p. 21 (check coupler after 50 mi)
Big Tex spec sheet (Demco EZ Latch 2-5/16)

r-lights.about: Check the trailer lights and wiring every trip and inspect the wiring yearly.
steps: Plug in the 7-pin. Run running lights, left and right turn, hazards and brake (use a helper).
Walk around: clearance and marker lights, tail lights, reflectors.
Fix any dead bulb or loose ground. Clean the plug contacts with a brush.
Look at the wiring harness along the frame for rubs, bare wire and loose clips.
Add dielectric grease to the connectors and secure the loose wiring with ties.
Log date and trailer miles.
safety: Do not cut or splice wiring near the brake magnet leads unless you know the wire colors.

r-ramps.about: Inspect the ramps, dovetail, deck bolts and hinges every 6 months. General guidance.
steps: Lower the ramps and dovetail. Look at the hinges, pins and springs.
Look at the welds for cracks, especially at the ramp hinges and the deck cross members.
Check that the ramp latches hold when stowed.
Tighten any loose deck bolts. Replace missing hardware.
Check the deck boards for rot or soft spots, especially around the bolts.
Lube the hinges and springs.
Log date and trailer miles.
safety: Keep fingers clear of the springs and hinges.
cite: Big Tex OM p. 55-56 (ramp secure top and bottom, stow and secure)

r-deck.about: Reseal the wood deck with penetrating oil every 6 to 12 months (company plan).
parts: Penetrating deck oil (trailer wood oil or linseed-type)
steps: Pick a dry day. Sweep the deck and wash off dirt. Let it dry.
Check for soft or rotted boards and replace them first.
Apply a thin coat of penetrating oil with a brush or roller, one board at a time. Do not leave puddles.
Wipe off the excess after about 20 minutes.
Let it dry per the can before loading.
Log date and trailer miles.
safety: Oily rags can self-heat. Spread them to dry or put them in a water-filled can.
A fresh oiled deck is slippery.
cite: Big Tex OM p. 55 (inspect deck, hold-downs and D-rings before loading)

r-tireage.about: Check the DOT date code on each trailer tire and plan to replace by 6 years from the date. The trailer was built Aug 2026.
specs: 6 years from the DOT date, sooner if cracked
7 years, to 10/5/2033. The shop must call the warranty company before work
steps: Find the DOT code on each sidewall. The last 4 digits are week and year (for example 2926 = week 29 of 2026).
Write down the date for each of the 4 tires and the spare.
Check for dry cracks, bulges and uneven wear.
Set a reminder for 6 years after the oldest date.
Before any tire work call the warranty company (see the Insurance tab).
safety: An old tire can fail even with good tread.
cite: Big Tex OM p. 67-68 (pressure loss 1-3 psi a month, inspect wheels yearly)

r-dot.about: Get the annual DOT inspection for the trailer along with the truck.
steps: Ask Totni whether they hold a trailer inspection report on file.
If not, have the trailer inspected at the same time as the truck (one visit).
Keep the report with the trailer papers and send a copy to Totni.
Fix any defects and log the date and shop here.
safety: Brake and light defects are the most common out-of-service items.

r-lug.about: Torque the trailer wheel nuts with a torque wrench: before the first road use and after any wheel removal, re-check at 10, 25, 50 and 100 miles, then every 3 months or 3,000 miles.
specs: 5/8-18 90 degree cone nut with clamp ring
Big Tex: 10, 25 and 50 mi (OM p. 59, 61). Dexter: 50 and 100 mi (p. 76). Do all of them
Every 3 months or 3,000 mi (Dexter p. 4), before each tow and at least twice a year (Big Tex p. 70)
Not confirmed. Look at the nuts: flat flange washer (flange nut) or tapered seat (cone). Wheel maker spec wins
steps: Identify the nut type first and pick the row. Do not guess the torque.
Trailer on the ground, chocked.
Start all nuts by hand, then tighten in stages in the 8-bolt star sequence (Dexter p. 75-76).
Final torque with a torque wrench. A 4-way or impact is for emergencies only (Big Tex p. 70).
Note any nut that lost torque. If one keeps losing torque, the studs, nuts, wheel or hub need a technician (Big Tex p. 70).
Log date and approximate trailer miles (Big Tex p. 70 asks for a record).
safety: A loose dual wheel can come off. Over-torque stretches studs.
r-lug.note: Earlier SOP used the 2-8K Dexter chart (9/16 studs, 140-170). Our 12K axles fall under the 9-15K manual.
cite: Dexter 9-15K p. 75-76 (sequence, torque by nut type, 50/100 mi re-check)
Big Tex OM p. 69-70 (torque wrench, keep a record)

r-breakaway.about: Test the breakaway switch and check the breakaway battery. Dexter: at every use. We use monthly plus before a long trip.
tools: Multimeter or the trailer's battery tester
parts: Breakaway battery or the correct 12V battery if weak
specs: Before every use (Big Tex OM p. 61; Dexter p. 4). We log it monthly
Pull the pin and try to pull forward: the trailer must resist. Put the pin back at once (Big Tex p. 48)
To the truck, pulls before the chains take up slack; never to a chain or the ball (p. 48)
If unused 3+ months or in winter: battery indoors, charge every 3 months (p. 48)
Never tow with the pin out
Brakes overheat and can fail for good (p. 48)
steps: Chock the trailer wheels.
Check the charge indicator light on the breakaway box (or measure the battery voltage).
Pull the pin with the trailer unplugged from the truck. The trailer brakes should lock (try to push or roll it).
Put the pin back in and confirm the brakes release.
Charge the battery if the test is weak, or replace it every couple of years.
Check the cable, clip and switch for wear and the box for water.
Log date and the result.
safety: Do the pull-pin test with wheels chocked so the trailer cannot roll.
cite: Big Tex OM p. 47-48 (test, lanyard, storage)
Big Tex OM p. 61 (before each use)

r-tires.about: Check the trailer tire pressure (80 psi cold) and condition before each trip and at least monthly.
specs: Cold, to the trailer VIN / certification label (Big Tex OM p. 58, 67). 80 psi for ST235/80R16 LRE
Weekly (Dexter p. 4) and before every trip (Big Tex p. 61)
Not driven 3 h, or under 1 mi after 3 h parked (Ram OM p. 327)
Pressure rises 2-6 psi when hot; never bleed hot tires (Ram OM p. 331)
The manuals give one cold pressure: the label value at GVWR. Run 80 psi loaded or empty
steps: Check pressures with a gauge when cold. Set each tire to 80 psi.
Look at the tread across the whole face for uneven wear (a sign of alignment or brake problems).
Look at both sidewalls for cuts, bulges or dry cracks. Look for nails.
Check the valve caps and the spare.
Check the lug nuts (see the lug item).
Log date and trailer miles. For tire damage call the warranty company first (Insurance tab).
safety: Do not exceed the tire sidewall maximum. Under-inflation overheats a loaded tire fast.
cite: Big Tex OM p. 58, 67-68 (label pressure, cold, 1-3 psi a month loss)
Ram OM p. 204-205, 327, 331 (trailer tires before towing; cold; heat rise)

r-magnets.about: Check the trailer brake magnets and the Ram brake controller output every 6 months or 6,000 miles.
specs: 6 months or 6,000 mi (Dexter p. 4; Big Tex OM p. 62)
Replace if uneven, or coil shows through the facing; replace in pairs per axle (Dexter p. 16)
Measure system and per-magnet current against the Dexter amperage chart (Dexter p. 21-22)
Ram ITBM GAIN 0-10 in 0.5 steps; Heavy Electric over 10,000 lb (OM p. 205-206)
steps: With the trailer hooked up, slide the manual lever fully and read the system amps at the trailer plug (Dexter p. 21-22).
Low or uneven amps: check grounds and connectors first (corrosion raises resistance).
With a drum off (do it with the hub service), lay a straightedge on each magnet face.
Replace worn magnets in pairs and reface the drum armature at the same time (Dexter p. 56).
Re-set GAIN on a dry lot at 20-25 mph (OM p. 206).
Log date, trailer miles and the amp readings.
safety: Use jack stands rated for the load. Never work under a vehicle held only by a jack.

r-brkyr.about: Yearly (or 12,000 mi) trailer brake inspection: shoes, drums, armature face, wiring. Big Tex says have the dealer inspect brakes and magnets at least once a year.
specs: 12 months or 12,000 mi (Dexter p. 4; Big Tex OM p. 62, 64-65)
Inspect for scoring and abnormal wear; reface armature when magnets are replaced (Dexter p. 55-56)
Dealer at least yearly (Big Tex p. 64-65)
steps: Book it with the hub bearing service (same teardown).
Inspect shoes and linings for wear or grease; drums for scoring.
Inspect magnets (see Brake magnets item) and the brake wiring for bare spots.
Clean with brake cleaner. Light grease on anchor pins and actuating arm only, never on linings (Dexter p. 15).
Adjust the brakes after reassembly.
Log date, trailer miles, shop and findings.
safety: Use jack stands rated for the load. Never work under a vehicle held only by a jack.
Brake dust is harmful: do not blow it with air.

r-susp.about: Inspect the trailer suspension every 6 months or 6,000 miles and re-torque any loose fasteners to the Dexter values.
specs: Suspension parts 6 months or 6,000 mi; springs and hanger welds 12 months (Dexter p. 4, 66)
Checked by the dealer yearly (Big Tex OM p. 62)
steps: Look at the springs for cracks, broken leaves or lost arch.
Look at the hangers and equalizers for cracked welds and elongated bolt holes.
Check the U-bolts and spring-eye bolts for looseness; torque only if loose or replaced (Dexter p. 66).
Check the HD adjustable suspension and the frame near the hangers.
Log date and trailer miles.
safety: Do not lift or support the trailer on the axle or suspension (Dexter p. 66).
Use jack stands rated for the load. Never work under a vehicle held only by a jack.
cite: Big Tex OM p. 62-63 (annual pro inspection, axle bolts by dealer)

r-jack.about: Grease the 50K two-speed landing gear (drop-leg jacks) once a year.
specs: Once a year (Big Tex OM p. 62, 67)
Grease fitting if present; else remove the top and pack the gears (p. 67)
steps: Lower the jacks a little to take load off the gears only if the trailer is supported safely.
Pump grease into each fitting until fresh grease shows.
If no fitting: remove the top cover and hand-pack the gears.
Crank through both speeds to spread the grease.
Log the date.
safety: Drop legs are spring loaded: keep feet and hands clear (Big Tex p. 46).
cite: Big Tex spec sheet (50K dual 2-speed landing gear)

r-rot.about: Rotate the trailer tires at 5,000 miles and look over tread and sidewalls.
specs: Rotate at 5,000 mi; tread and sidewall check every 6 months or 6,000 mi (Big Tex OM p. 62)
Wheel nut re-check at 10, 25, 50 mi (Big Tex p. 59)
Call the warranty company before any tire work
steps: Check cold pressures first.
Mark positions with chalk.
Jack by the frame, set stands; move wheels front to rear on the same side (general practice).
Torque the nuts (see Lug nut item) and set 80 psi cold.
Re-check nut torque at 10, 25 and 50 mi.
Log date and trailer miles.
safety: Use jack stands rated for the load. Never work under a vehicle held only by a jack.
r-rot.note: The rotation pattern is general guidance; the interval is from the Big Tex manual.

r-s5.about: Care for the on-hand S5 Coupler Locks steel box sleeve and Trimax THP XL puck lock. The sleeve fits over the Demco yellow gooseneck coupler and the puck lock goes in the side shroud.
parts: None. The S5 sleeve and Trimax THP XL puck lock are already on hand.
specs: Install the S5 sleeve and lock the Trimax THP XL puck lock in the side shroud
Remove the sleeve and puck lock and stow them in the gooseneck toolbox
Keep the working key off the trailer. Keep a spare key at home. Do not write or store key codes in this app or on the trailer
Every 3 months, or if the puck lock feels sticky. Use graphite or a dry lock lube, not a wet oil that collects dirt
steps: Before hitching, unlock the puck lock, slide the S5 sleeve off the Demco coupler, and stow the sleeve and lock in the gooseneck toolbox.
After you unhook or drop the trailer, slide the S5 steel box sleeve over the Demco coupler so it covers the latch.
Put the Trimax THP XL puck lock in the side shroud and lock it. Tug the sleeve to confirm it cannot come off.
Lube the puck lock with graphite or a dry lock lubricant. Wipe off extra. Do this at least every 3 months.
Keep the working key off the trailer (on the key ring or in the truck, not in the toolbox).
Keep a spare key at home.
Do not write, photograph, or store the key code in this app, on the trailer, or in the toolbox.
Log the lube date here.
safety: Never hitch with the S5 sleeve still on the coupler. It can damage the coupler, the sleeve, and the truck hitch.
A trailer left unhooked without the coupler lock is an easy theft target.
r-s5.note: Key codes are not stored in this app.
cite: On-hand equipment (S5 Coupler Locks sleeve, Trimax THP XL puck lock). Key codes are not stored.

docs: 2026 Ram HD Payload and Towing chart
ratings: Ram tow chart (Mega Cab DRW 4x4 HO)
Ram tow chart (Mega Cab DRW HO 3.42)
On the door label (not yet on file)
60% of cargo in the front half

fit.title: Fit rule vs. the ratings (rule unchanged)
rows: 14,000 - 10,940 (CAT) = 3,060 lb for the cargo share on the truck
3,060 / 0.25 = 12,240 lb: just under the 12,500 OK line
About 4,800-5,250 lb, under the 5,565 lb hitch rating
fit.note: This holds only if the 10,940 lb CAT reading was the truck axles with the empty trailer hooked up. If it was the truck alone, the pin of a loaded trailer would push the truck over 14,000 lb well before 12,500 lb of cargo. Scale the first heavy load: steer, drive and trailer axles.

insights: Ram lug torque is in the manual
DRW flanged M14 nuts, 22 mm: 134-149 ft-lb (142 nominal). Retighten after 25 miles.
Dexter: grease or hub oil every 12 months or 12,000 mi, not 15,000. Hub item moved up.
Adjust after the first 200 mi and every 3,000 mi. No record of the 200 mi job.
Big Tex OM p. 59; Dexter p. 4-5
Trailer: 10, 25, 50 (and Dexter 100) mi after any wheel off. Applies after the 11/11 warranty wheel and tire exchange at Big Tex in Jacksonville.
Big Tex OM p. 59; Dexter p. 76
Flange nut 275-325, swivel flange 150-175, cone with clamp ring 190-210 ft-lb. Old SOP used the light-duty 140-170.
Inspect every 15,000 mi or 12 months; never past 30,000 mi or 24 months.
Time limits on every Ram item
The diesel plan has months too: rotation 6, fuel filters 12, brakes 18, bearings 24, trans 48.
TOW/HAUL for all towing; exhaust brake off on ice; no cruise on hills or heavy loads.
Big Tex: generally never over 60 mph towing. Ram: 50 mph max on a full-size spare.
Big Tex OM p. 21; Ram OM p. 204
Idle 3-5 min after full load or climbing before shutdown; avoid long idles (soot, regen).
At 70% full the cluster asks for highway driving; never let it reach 100% (dealer cleaning).
Block heater below 0 F, required below -20 F, 1+ h. Below 20 F use winter blend or treatment. DEF freezes at 12 F.
Gooseneck pin 20-25% of loaded trailer; 60% of cargo in the front half; low and centered.
No towing first 500 mi; first 500 towing mi under 50 mph. Cummins needs no special engine break-in. Long past for us.
Ram: retain all receipts. Big Tex: log every lug torque check with date and miles.
Ram OM p. 287; Big Tex OM p. 70
Mega Cab is 31 gal (the trip planner used 32). Planner fixed to 31 gal, 30 gal fills.
